content: 1. If the mother is HIV-infected, provide her with the appropriate antiretroviral treatment and ensure the newborn receives necessary prophylaxis. 2. In cases of heavy vaginal bleeding, palpate the uterus. If the uterus is not firm, perform fundal massage to encourage contraction and expel any clots. 3. If the bleeding is severe and a pad is soaked in less than 5 minutes, manage the situation as a medical emergency and refer to hospital care if necessary. 4. If the bleeding originates from a perineal tear, repair the tear or refer the patient to a hospital for further management. 5. Encourage the mother to empty her bladder and ensure she has passed urine. If she is unable to urinate or the bladder is distended, assist her by gently pouring water over the vulva. Avoid catheterization unless absolutely necessary. 6. Review the medical record and administer any due treatments or prophylaxis. 7. Provide the mother with advice on postpartum care, including hygiene, nutrition, and when to seek medical attention. 8. Counsel the mother on birth spacing and family planning methods, ensuring she understands the options available to her. 9. Conduct a thorough examination of the mother before discharge, assessing her condition after delivery. 10. If the mother desires tubal ligation or an intrauterine device (IUD), make the necessary arrangements before discharge. 11. After an uncomplicated vaginal delivery, both the mother and newborn should remain in the healthcare facility for at least 24 hours for observation and care. 12. Examine the mother one hour after delivery or later, checking for signs of complications such as excessive bleeding, uterine firmness, and perineal tears. 13. Monitor the mother’s temperature, blood pressure, and overall condition, ensuring there are no signs of infection, pallor, or other abnormalities. 14. If the mother exhibits signs of heavy bleeding, fever, or elevated blood pressure, manage these conditions promptly and refer to a hospital if necessary. 15. For uterine or fetal infections, administer intravenous fluids and appropriate antibiotics, and refer the patient urgently to a hospital. 16. If the mother has severe anemia (hemoglobin <7 g/dL), refer her urgently to a hospital for intensive monitoring and management. 17. If the mother is severely ill or separated from her baby, assist her in expressing breast milk every three hours to ensure the baby receives adequate nutrition. 18. In the event of a stillbirth or neonatal death, provide supportive care to the parents, including discussing the events leading to the death and offering privacy to grieve. 19. Advise the mother on postpartum hygiene, including washing hands before handling the baby, cleaning the perineum daily, and changing perineal pads regularly. 20. Counsel the mother on proper nutrition, encouraging her to eat a variety of healthy foods to regain strength and support breastfeeding. 21. Discuss family planning options with the mother, emphasizing the importance of birth spacing and the use of contraceptive methods suitable for her situation. 22. Advise the mother on the importance of safer sex practices, including the use of condoms to prevent sexually transmitted infections and unintended pregnancies. 23. Encourage the mother to attend routine postpartum visits and to seek immediate medical attention if danger signs such as severe bleeding, fever, or abdominal pain occur. 24. Discuss emergency preparedness with the mother and her family, including identifying where to go for care, how to reach the hospital, and the costs involved. 25. Record all treatments and findings in the mother’s medical record and ensure proper follow-up care is arranged. 26. If the mother is HIV-positive, support adherence to antiretroviral therapy and ensure the newborn receives appropriate treatment. 27. Provide preventive measures such as tetanus immunization, iron supplementation, and counseling on the use of insecticide-treated bed nets. 28. Advise the mother to avoid inserting anything into the vagina, abstain from sexual intercourse until the perineal wound heals, and ensure adequate rest and sleep. 29. Counsel the mother on avoiding tobacco, alcohol, and drug use, and encourage family members to support her in maintaining a healthy environment. 30. For breastfeeding mothers, explain the lactational amenorrhea method (LAM) as a temporary contraceptive option and discuss additional family planning methods if desired. 31. Encourage the mother to bring her partner or a family member to at least one postpartum visit to support her care and decision-making. 32. Advise the mother to monitor for danger signs such as excessive bleeding, convulsions, difficulty breathing, or severe depression, and to seek immediate medical care if these occur. 33. Discuss the importance of postpartum home visits by community health workers to ensure the well-being of both the mother and newborn.
